solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ignite vessel secured by chain to land

indicators.note: the vessel is held fast by the chain, which follows straight after it

parts.note: a cat is an old name for a type of sailing vessel, and short for catamaran
CH is the standard abbreviation for chain, a surveyor's length
to light is to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A boat is made fast by its chain before it comes ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignite' looks like an odd instruction, but it is the definition, read as a two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch light is an idiom for starting to burn, so it is a phrase meaning to ignite.

clue.text: Ballet move is better with one in position

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: the numeral one is placed inside the word for position

parts.note: a role is a position or job
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dancer claims a step improves when performed by one in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriole is a leap in ballet, a caper in the air; it is a specific dance movement.

clue.text: Country medical program shown in school

indicators.note: the medical programme appears inside the word for school, as if shown within it

parts.note: to train is to school or teach
ER is the long-running American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: A national medical programme is being screened in a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Country in the sense of land or landscape, as in hill country, is a synonym of terrain.

clue.text: Relocation of North Sea oil concerning high-ranking British naval officer

indicators.note: relocation moves things about, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

parts.note: on means about or concerning, as in a talk on history

explanation.surface: A naval commander takes a view on moving North Sea oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Lord Nelson, victor at Trafalgar, is the most famous high-ranking officer of Britain's Royal Navy.

clue.text: Rascal wandered around island unprepared

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal

indicators.note: the word for wandered goes around the island abbreviation

parts.note: roved means wandered or roamed

explanation.surface: A scamp roamed round an island without any preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improvised is done on the spur of the moment, without preparation, so it is unprepared.

clue.text: The sound made by caught animals

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken like the word that follows

parts.note: to have caught a remark is to have heard it

explanation.surface: Trapped creatures make a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like trapping animals; it means picking up a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a group of animals such as cattle, so it stands for animals collectively.

clue.text: Ingredients of recipe — assorted vegetables

indicators.note: Ingredients of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recipe calls for a mixture of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas are green seeds eaten as a vegetable, so they are an example of vegetables.

clue.text: Solitary leaf dropped by diseased lime tree

indicators.note: a diseased tree is out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the tree loses the letter for leaf, as a tree drops a leaf

explanation.surface: A single leaf falls from a sickly lime tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped by' removes L from LIMETREE, leaving IMETREE, which 'diseased' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary as a noun is a recluse, and an eremite is a religious hermit living alone.

clue.text: Keep quiet about warm jacket

indicators.note: the call for silence goes about, around, the word for warm

parts.note: SH is the command to keep quiet
to heat is to warm

explanation.surface: Someone is told to say nothing about a cosy jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting covering or casing, a jacket in the mechanical sense.

clue.text: Head of pathology reassembled rare knife

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the letters of the word rare are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: The chief pathologist puts together an unusual scalpel.
explanation.definitionFit: A parer is a small knife used for paring fruit or vegetables.

clue.text: Keep going as such, moving around at all times

parts.note: per se is Latin for as such, in itself

indicators.note: a letter moves round from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: ever means always, at all times

explanation.surface: Advice to keep moving about constantly, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving around' shifts the opening letter of the always-word to its end; 'Keep going' is the definition, not part of the surface's advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist and carry on despite difficulty, synonymous with keeping going.

clue.text: Court specialist's sex tips weren't out of line

indicators.note: things out of line are disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist's advice on sex, offered in court, was quite proper.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert witness gives specialist opinion evidence in a court of law.

clue.text: Operative's lack of mobility

definitions.meaning: operative means working, in operation, as a phrase of two words
idleness or a failure to move or act

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer means operative; read as one it means lack of mobility. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a state of not acting or moving, a lack of mobility or activity.

clue.text: One left in an awkward situation messed up

indicators.note: the letters for one and left sit inside the word for a tricky situation

parts.note: to be in a spot is to be in an awkward situation
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person abandoned in a tricky situation was ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilt means ruined or damaged, a synonym of messed up.

clue.text: Spanish talkers — they are difficult to understand

parts.note: SP is the abbreviation for Spanish
utterers are people who speak, talkers

explanation.surface: Speakers of Spanish can be hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: People who splutter or speak in jerky bursts are hard to understand; such speakers are described by the definition.

clue.text: Language matter supported by liberal in government

indicators.note: the matter held up inside these words is a run of letters hidden within them

explanation.surface: Language policy is backed by a Liberal politician in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is an informal word for a language or jargon, especially a foreign one.

clue.text: Acknowledgement by one who's separated is passed on

parts.note: someone owning up to a state says I am, shortened to I'm
parted means separated

explanation.surface: A divorcee's admission is passed along.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one person admitting they are separated. The 'is' before the definition is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart information is to pass it on or communicate it.

clue.text: Cover beet growing on both sides of tumbledown shed

indicators.note: the beet grows round both sides of the jumbled shed, enclosing it
a tumbledown shed is falling apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's beetroot is growing round a ramshackle shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbledown' jumbles the shed's letters, and 'growing on both sides of' has the vegetable wrap round them; 'Cover' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsheet is a linen cover laid over a bed.

clue.text: Fertiliser kept in club's cellar

indicators.note: the fertiliser is kept inside the word for club

parts.note: a bat is a club, as used in cricket or baseball; the 's is a link
semen is the fluid that fertilises an egg

explanation.surface: Fertiliser is being stored in a golf club's cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is a storey below ground level, much like a cellar.

clue.text: Gold part going around top of evangelist's halo

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the word for part goes around the first letter of evangelist

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A golden ring sits around the head of a gospel writer as a halo.
explanation.definitionFit: An aureole is a circle of light round a holy figure's head, a halo.

clue.text: Was core picked out of the rubbish?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word the is removed, like coring an apple

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the apple core was taken out of the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at an apple core in the bin; here the core is the middle letter of a short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste means rubbish or refuse, material that has been thrown away.

clue.text: Stock sleep in one

indicators.note: the word for sleep is placed inside the word for one

parts.note: sole means single, only one
kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: Livestock are asleep together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' as a ski pole is from the German Stock, stick; it is a rare sense in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock here is a stick or staff, as in alpenstock, so it names a skier's pole.

clue.text: Call girl forcefully cut off part

indicators.note: the word for forcefully has its final letter cut off

parts.note: hard means with force, forcefully
a lot is a portion or share, a part

explanation.surface: A girl on the phone abruptly ends her share of the call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call girl' looks like part of the telephone story; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlot is an old word for a prostitute, the same trade as a call girl.

clue.text: Stopped a run in game of cricket

indicators.note: the run abbreviation goes inside the word for the cricket match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
R is the scoring abbreviation for run in cricket

explanation.surface: A single run was cut short in a cricket Test.
explanation.definitionFit: At rest means motionless, no longer moving, which is to say stopped.

clue.text: Lookouts dispatched by one locked in residence

parts.note: sent means dispatched

indicators.note: the numeral one is locked inside the residence abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Guards were sent off after someone was locked in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries are soldiers posted on watch, which makes them lookouts.

clue.text: Strip of vinyl in ordinary floor covering

indicators.note: a strip taken from these words is a run of their letters hidden across them

explanation.surface: A strip of vinyl makes ordinary flooring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lino, short for linoleum, is a hard-wearing sheet floor covering.

clue.text: Served with onions, side of lamb is eaten by anyone in a mess

indicators.note: one side of the word lamb is its first letter
letters in a mess are jumbled, so these are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Lamb with onions is served to everyone in the officers' mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served with onions' looks like anagram fodder but is the culinary definition; 'eaten by' only says the lamb's letter and 'is' join the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyonnaise is the French culinary term for food cooked or served with onions.

clue.text: Excited people, slipping quietly away, run off together

indicators.note: excited people are stirred up, so the letters are mixed
slipping away means the letter for quietly leaves the word
away completes the sense of departing, with the letter gone

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Thrilled lovers sneak off quietly to run away together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping quietly away' removes P from PEOPLE, leaving EOPLE for 'Excited' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is for a couple to run off together secretly to marry.

clue.text: Bear pelt

definitions.meaning: an archaic verb sense: to give birth, to bring forth young
to pelt is to rain very heavily

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns for animal and fur; both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Teem once meant to bear offspring, and now means to pour with rain, to pelt down.

clue.text: Subject matter entered by family member is true to principles

indicators.note: the family member goes into the word for subject matter

parts.note: content is the subject matter of a work
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A relative breaks into the subject of a principled discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being consistent means acting in line with the same principles each time, steady and unchanging.
